definition: Tree rearrangements are deterministic algorithms devoted to search for optimal phylogenetic tree structure.
details: They can be applied to any set of data that are naturally arranged into a tree, but have most applications in computational phylogenetics, especially in maximum parsimony and maximum likelihood searches of phylogenetic trees, which seek to identify one among many possible trees that best explains the evolutionary history of a particular gene or species.
story: Picture an engineer at a cluttered workbench, turning a clever idea over in their hands until it finally clicks. Think of it this way: Tree rearrangements are deterministic algorithms devoted to search for optimal phylogenetic tree structure. And here is the clever part: They can be applied to any set of data that are naturally arranged into a tree, but have most applications in computational phylogenetics, especially in maximum parsimony and maximum likelihood searches of phylogenetic trees, which seek to identify one among many possible trees that best explains the evolutionary history of a particular gene or species. It is one of those ideas that feels obvious only after someone shows it to you. That is Tree rearrangement — a small key that opens a big door.
